title: CrowdStrike’s Zscaler deal aims to give security teams a single kill switch for rogue AI agents
summary:
CrowdStrike's AI kill switch can cut off access to AI models at the AI gateway today. The company agreed on Monday to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock deal valued at about $43.9 billion, and it plans to take that kill switch onto the network, where AI agents travel between the device and the cloud.

title: Nearly half of surveyed engineers and leaders say the AI agents that write their code also review it
summary:
As AI coding tools generate more code, review has become a constraint on how fast that code ships. But only 26% of respondents to a new survey say they are very confident they understand AI-generated changes as thoroughly as human-written ones.

summary:

title: Tidal will start banning AI-generated music next month
summary:
Tidal is officially banning AI-generated music on December 9th. As a result of this change, Tidal will delete around 29 million AI-generated songs and reject an estimated 80,000 to 85,000 tracks per day, according to Tidal music lead Robert Andersen.
The move comes just months after Tidal began labeling and demonetizing tracks identified as 100 percent AI-generated. In a post on X, Andersen says Tidal needed to take a more "drastic" measure, as AI music made up 43 percent of the tracks distributed to the platform in the last 90 days. summary:

title: Z.ai's GLM-5.4 aims to match models up to four times its size by running 28 layers twice
summary:
GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship built on a Loop Transformer architecture, which reuses the same layers more than once instead of stacking new ones, so the model gets more depth and more computation per token without adding parameters. Thinking Machines Lab used a looped transformer in its Inkling 2 Mini model, which was released last week.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is back. What happens next?
summary:
After the leather-jacketed CEO, president, and co-founder of Nvidia, Jensen Huang, acknowledged an affair with Megaspeed exec Alice Huang, his company initially announced an investigation. However, after The New York Times reported there was evidence of another affair, this time with an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him, a board meeting that night ended with Huang’s resignation, and Nvidia CFO Colette Kress was installed as the new interim CEO.
And then… Huang was back. 
In recent years, Nvidia has become a key part of the Trump administration’s AI push, a central figure in negotiations over potential Chinese access to cutting-edge AI hardware, and a company that has used its now $4 trillion-plus market cap to finance other AI companies. Saying it received input “from senior levels of the United States government,” Nvidia’s board announced his return as CEO on November 23rd, less than two weeks after his resignation.

title: Claude Fable 5.2 cost three times as much as Opus 5.5 for nearly the same results in a VentureBeat bug-fixing test
summary:
Claude Fable 5.2, Anthropic's top model, passed 10 of 15 bug-fix tries in a VentureBeat pilot test at a total cost of about $89. Opus 5.5 passed 9 of 15 at a total cost of about $29. A one-pass gap is too small to call, so the two finished about the same amount of work, and Fable cost about three times as much in total. No model, at any price, passed the hardest task.
